senses.gloss: the base that others build on
gloss_distractors: a backup copy of the data
senses.definition: The base layer that other systems are built on and depend on.
senses.caution: It sounds grand and claims other systems really depend on it, which people can check. Used about another team's product, it can make their work sound minor.
senses.example: Identity and audit are substrate. Nobody should be building either of them per product.

cues.text: You are arguing that authentication and logging get built once as a base that every product team builds on top of, and you want the technical word for that base.
A director asks what the platform team actually delivers, and you want a word for the layer everything else simply assumes is there.
In an architecture review you want to name the foundation that would have to be replaced first if you ever changed cloud providers.
Talking with a friend about how much of daily life is built on the electricity grid, you want a word for a base that everything else depends on and nobody notices.
You are describing a shared language as the thing an entire culture's humour is built on top of.

distractors: A voluntary group of people doing the same work who meet to trade what they learn.
Temporary structure that holds work up until the real thing can stand on its own.
A number or a call given straight, with all the caveats stripped out of it.
To avoid something deliberately and on principle.
Low in a way that has given up on things improving.
